question:
Nonzero real numbers \(x,\) \(y,\) \(a,\) and \(b\) satisfy \(x < a\) and \(y < b.\) How many of the following inequalities must be true?

(I) \(x + y \lt a + b\)

(II) \(x - y \lt a - b\)

(III) \(xy \lt ab\)

(IV) \(\dfrac{x}{y} \lt \dfrac{a}{b}\)
solution:
A statement that must be true needs to hold for every allowed choice of the numbers. One allowed counterexample is enough to show that a statement need not hold.

Statement (I) always holds: adding \(y\) to \(x<a\), and then using \(y<b\), gives
\[
x+y<a+y<a+b.
\]
For the other statements, choose
\[
x=y=-2,\qquad a=b=-1.
\]
All four numbers are nonzero, and they satisfy \(x<a\) and \(y<b\). For these values:

(II) is false because \(x-y=a-b=0\), whereas the proposed inequality is strict.

(III) is false because \(xy=4\) and \(ab=1\), so \(xy>ab\).

(IV) is false because \(\frac{x}{y}=\frac{a}{b}=1\), again giving equality instead of a strict inequality. Both denominators are nonzero.

Thus only statement (I) must be true. The number is \(1\), choice B.

nodes.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems. nodes.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns, and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane. For example, given the rule “Add 3” and the starting number 0, and given the rule “Add 6” and the starting number 0, generate terms in the resulting sequences, and observe that the terms in one sequence are twice the corresponding terms in the other sequence. Explain informally why this is so.

nodes.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them. For example, express the calculation “add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2” as 2 × (8 + 7).
